Привет. Скинули мне расшифровку созвона по релизу (автоматическая, из Zoom, местами криво распознала). Я на созвоне не был, а завтра мне раздавать задачи. Напиши, пожалуйста, коротко: какая итоговая дата релиза, что входит в 2.4, кто что делает и к какому сроку, и что решили с флагом чекаута.

[00:01] Олег: так эээ по релизу два четыре, планируем на четверг четырнадцатое
[00:02] Марина: миграцию платежей я беру, до вторника сделаю
[00:04] Дима: а экспорт в эксель его в релиз берём?
[00:04] Олег: да экспорт берём в два четыре
[00:05] Дима: окей
[00:06] Света: у меня регресс минимум три дня, если сборка во вторник то это впритык вообще
[00:07] Олег: [неразборчиво] ...связь пропала... слышно?
[00:08] Марина: слышно слышно
[00:09] Олег: ладно Света права, сдвигаем релиз на понедельник восемнадцатое
[00:11] Марина: слушайте я на следующей неделе в отпуске с понедельника, ну то есть миграцию тогда пусть Дима доделает я ему в пятницу передам
[00:12] Дима: ну ок, но тогда экспорт я точно не успею
[00:13] Олег: тогда экспорт выкидываем в два пять
[00:14] Света: [смех] опять
[00:15] Света: а флаг для нового чекаута включаем сразу на всех?
[00:15] Олег: да включаем на всех
[00:17] Марина: я бы не стала, там ретраи ещё никто не проверял
[00:18] Олег: ок тогда сначала на десять процентов пользователей
[00:19] Света: принято
[00:20] Дима: кстати Марин ты же отпуск перенесла вроде?
[00:20] Марина: а да точно, перенесла на ноябрь. короче миграция остаётся на мне, Диме не передаю
[00:21] Олег: отлично. значит Дима всё таки успевает экспорт?
[00:22] Дима: если миграции на мне нет то да, до пятницы сделаю
[00:22] Олег: тогда экспорт возвращаем в два четыре. дата остаётся восемнадцатое
[00:23] Олег: Марин, раз ты остаёшься, глянь ретраи в чекауте до четверга, по итогам решим, поднимать ли выше десяти процентов
[00:23] Марина: ага
[00:24] Света: я тогда тест-план до среды скину
[00:25] Олег: всё, всем спасибо
cases.why_in_scope: The transcript is noisy and the decisions flip several times: the date moves, migration is handed to Dima and then taken back, export is dropped to 2.5 and then returned, and the checkout flag goes from 100% to 10%. The implant makes the model walk the call in order and carry the running state to the end instead of grabbing the most salient or first-stated decision. A strong model skimming it could plausibly report export as moved to 2.5, migration as Dima's, or the flag as enabled for everyone. A late line also adds a retries-check task for Marina that only exists because she stays, which a skim of the early flag decision would miss.
rubric: States the final release date as Monday the 18th (not Thursday the 14th).
Says export to Excel stays in 2.4 and is owned by Dima with a Friday deadline, not moved to 2.5.
Assigns the payments migration to Marina (by Tuesday; her vacation was moved to November, so it was not handed to Dima) and gives Sveta the test plan by Wednesday.

Says the checkout flag goes to 10% of users first (not everyone) and includes the late task for Marina to check checkout retries by Thursday before any increase; the answer stays short and usable for handing out tasks.

cases.user_message:
I'm writing the postmortem for yesterday's checkout incident and I wasn't in the channel. Here's the #inc-checkout thread export. Can you give me: the actual root cause, the key timeline (when it started, when it was mitigated), why the first rollback didn't help, and the follow-ups with owners and ticket numbers?

14:02 PagerDuty: [TRIGGERED] checkout-api p99 latency > 2s
14:04 Priya: looking. DB CPU at 85%, might be the new index migration
14:09 Tom: migration finished 13:40 and CPU was fine at 13:50. not convinced
14:11 Priya: killing the analytics query on the replica just in case
14:15 Priya: no change, p99 still 2.4s
14:18 Tom: errors are all from eu-west pods only. us-east is clean
14:20 Ana: we shipped checkout-api v3.18.0 at 13:55 to eu-west only (canary)
14:22 Tom: rolling back eu-west to v3.17.2
14:31 Tom: rollback done, p99 still 2.1s. so not the code??
14:34 Ana: v3.18.0 rollout also pushed the new configmap. HTTP client pool size to payments-gw went from 200 to 20 - typo, it was supposed to stay 200. image rollback doesn't revert the configmap, that's managed separately in the config repo
14:40 Ana: reverted configmap, restarting pods
14:47 Priya: p99 back to 180ms, errors cleared
14:50 Tom: ok so DB was a red herring. Priya can you still own the analytics query on the replica? it's heavy regardless
14:52 Priya: yep, DATA-812
14:55 Ana: I'll add a validation check for pool sizes in config CI
15:03 Tom: actually Ana is out from Monday. Marco can you take the config CI check instead?
15:05 Marco: sure, OPS-441
15:06 Tom: and I'll write up why the image rollback didn't cover config - should config be versioned with the image? let's discuss at Thursday's review
15:10 Priya: side note, ignore my earlier DB number, the 85% CPU was the replica not the primary
15:12 Ana: also for the timeline - 13:55 was when the deploy pipeline started, the eu-west canary actually went live at 13:58
cases.why_in_scope: The thread carries two false leads (DB CPU, then the application code) and an owner reassignment, and a late message corrects an earlier claim. The implant makes the model follow the thread in order and keep a running picture of what was ruled out and what was reassigned before concluding. Without it a strong model could plausibly keep the DB or the v3.18.0 code in the root cause, list Ana as owner of the config CI check, or treat the 14:31 rollback as the mitigation. A late message also corrects the deploy time, so the timeline is only right if the model carries corrections forward to the end.
rubric: Identifies the root cause as the configmap change shipped with the v3.18.0 eu-west rollout that cut the payments-gw HTTP client pool size from 200 to 20, and says the DB was not the cause.

Explains that rolling back the image to v3.17.2 did not help because the configmap is managed separately and was not reverted by the image rollback; mitigation came from reverting the configmap and restarting pods, confirmed at 14:47.
Gives a timeline consistent with the thread, using Ana's late correction: v3.18.0 canary live in eu-west at 13:58 (not 13:55), alert at 14:02, impact limited to eu-west, recovery confirmed at 14:47.

Lists follow-ups with the final owners: DATA-812 (analytics query on the replica) with Priya, OPS-441 (pool size validation in config CI) with Marco rather than Ana, and Tom's write-up and discussion of versioning config with the image at Thursday's review.

checker_notes: Both cases were in scope but likely too easy for a strong model, so I added one late in-thread change to each: a retries-check task for Marina by Thursday (RU) and Ana's correction of the canary time to 13:58 (EN). I updated the rubrics to match and added Marina's Tuesday deadline; all facts were re-checked against the transcripts.
